text: dsh-vitals（DSH 插件，网页客户端）：在 DSH 网页界面显示主机硬件的实时状态。它在主机侧读取 CPU、内存、温度和 GPU 指标，并通过网页数据路由提供给客户端；界面包含会话标题栏的迷你负载组件，以及 Chat 和 Trajectory 旁的 Hardware 面板。主要功能有 CPU 总体与每核负载、内存使用量、可用温度读数，以及 GPU 温度、利用率、功耗和显存。适合运行 DSH 网页界面并希望查看本机硬件负载的用户。无需 API 密钥或账号；GPU 数据取决于主机可用的硬件工具。
dsh-vitals monitors host hardware in the DSH web UI. Its Hardware panel and session-header widget show CPU load, memory, temperatures, and available GPU metrics. No API key or account is needed.

dsh-vitals 的功能「CPU 与内存面板」：Hardware 面板显示总体及每核 CPU 负载、CPU 型号和内存已用量，并以历史曲线呈现平滑后的 CPU 负载。
dsh-vitals 的功能「GPU 状态卡片」：Hardware 面板为检测到的 GPU 显示温度、利用率、功耗和显存；可用字段缺失时以占位内容呈现。
dsh-vitals 的功能「标题栏迷你负载组件」：会话标题栏显示 CPU 与 GPU 负载概览，点击可切换到完整 Hardware 面板。

dsh-vitals README · Introduction：A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh) web GUI plugin that shows **live hardware load** right where you work: a self-contained, dependency-free companion to `btop`. Watch your GPU while your local model thinks, without leaving the chat.

```bash
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-vitals
```

dsh-vitals README · Introduction：No restart needed (the web profile reloads live). Reload the browser tab: CPU and GPU load appear in the session header, and the full **Hardware** tab sits next to Chat / Trajectory. Full details under [Install](#install).

dsh-vitals README · Introduction：


The mini widget in the session header: always visible while you chat. Click it to jump to the full Hardware tab.

dsh-vitals README · What it shows：- **CPU** — overall utilisation, a live 60s sparkline, highest temperature reading, and per-core load (every physical core, any count) — with per-thermal-zone detail when there's more than one sensor
- **Memory** — used / available / total with utilisation %
- **GPUs** — one card each: name, temperature, utilisation, power draw, and VRAM (used / total)

Data is sampled host-side on every poll (~0.5 s) and rendered live.

dsh-vitals README · How it works：- **Host** — a `GET`-only route registered on the dsh web server
  (`/plugins/dsh-vitals/data`) that reads the OS's own sources
  with **no privileged access** and returns JSON.
- **Client** — a single self-contained bundle that polls the route and draws
  the panels with inline styles (no CSS pipeline, no assets).

dsh-vitals README · Where it shows up：Two access points, both live the moment the plugin is bundled — no setup:

- **A mini widget in the session header**, next to the "⋯" menu: CPU and
  per-GPU load as tiny bars, always visible while you chat. Hover for temps
  and VRAM; click to jump to the full tab.
- **A full `Hardware` tab** next to **Chat** / **Trajectory** at the top of
  the conversation view: per-core CPU, memory, temperatures and every GPU.

dsh-vitals README · Platform support：Linux, macOS and Windows. Each signal uses the best unprivileged source the OS
offers and hides itself when there is none. Linux is tested live; the macOS and
Windows readers are only checked against sample output (`npm test`) so far.
Reports from real Macs and Windows machines are very welcome.

dsh-vitals README · Platform support：| Signal | Linux | macOS | Windows |
| ------ | ----- | ----- | ------- |
| CPU load (overall + per core) | `/proc/stat` | `os.cpus()` | `os.cpus()` |
| Memory | `/proc/meminfo` | `vm_stat` (counts cache as available, like Activity Monitor) | `os.freemem()` |
| CPU temperature | `/sys/class/thermal` | hidden (needs root) | WMI thermal zones, when the board exposes them (often needs dsh running as admin) |
| NVIDIA GPUs | `nvidia-smi` | `nvidia-smi` | `nvidia-smi.exe` (PATH or `NVSMI` folder) |
| Apple / other GPUs | — | `ioreg` utilisation + memory in use | — |

dsh-vitals README · Platform support：Everything degrades gracefully: a missing source hides that panel or shows a
placeholder instead of breaking the tab. Any number of GPUs and any CPU core
count is supported.

dsh-vitals README · Install：Into your dsh **web profile** (`web` below is the profile name; use whichever
profile backs your web GUI). From a source checkout, use `pnpm dsh` instead of
`npx @deepseek-ai/dsh`:

```bash
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-vitals
```

dsh-vitals README · Install：This installs the package into the profile and adds it to
`dsh.profile.bundles` for you — no manual `package.json` editing. (No local
`dsh` binary? Run the equivalent by hand from the profile directory, e.g.
`~/.dsh/profiles/web/`: `pnpm add dsh-vitals`, then add `"dsh-vitals"` to
that `package.json`'s `dsh.profile.bundles` array yourself.)

The published package ships its built `lib/` output, so no build step runs
on install.

dsh-vitals README · Install：No restart: the shipped `web` profile reloads live, so the plugin shows up under
**Plugins** right away. Reload the browser tab — see
[Where it shows up](#where-it-shows-up) above for how to find it.

dsh-vitals README · Building from source：Requires Node 20+. Dependencies are dev-only (esbuild); the published package
has **zero runtime npm dependencies**.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/JoblessJoe/dsh-vitals.git
cd dsh-vitals
pnpm install
node scripts/build.mjs     # emits lib/index.js + lib/client.js

`package.json` declares a `build` script, so `pnpm build` works too.
dsh-vitals README · Configuration：None. The plugin reads whatever the host exposes; there is no config surface.

dsh-vitals README · Security：The data route sits outside the dsh web server's `/api` trust fence, so it
enforces that fence itself: `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` requests are rejected
(403) and only `GET`/`HEAD` are served (405 otherwise). All sources are read-only.
